s:
Consider the following statements about the Speakers of the Lok Sabha:
1. M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar was the first Deputy Speaker and later the Speaker of the 2nd Lok Sabha.
2. Sumitra Mahajan was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
3. N. Sanjiva Reddy is the only Lok Sabha Speaker who became President of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Meira Kumar (2009-14) was the first woman Speaker; Sumitra Mahajan (2014-19) was the second. Ayyangar was the first Deputy Speaker (1952-56) and Speaker of the 2nd LS; N. Sanjiva Reddy is the only Speaker who became President (1977).

s:
Match List-I (Office in Andhra Pradesh) with List-II (First holder):
List-I
a. Speaker of the first AP Legislative Assembly (1956)
b. Deputy Speaker of the first AP Legislative Assembly (1956)
c. Chairman of the AP Legislative Council
d. Woman Speaker of the AP Legislative Assembly (11th Assembly)
List-II
i. Madapati Hanumantha Rao
ii. K. Prathibha Bharathi
iii. Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
iv. Kalluri Subbarao
x: First AP Legislature (1956): Speaker Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao, Deputy Speaker Kalluri Subbarao; first Council Chairman Madapati Hanumantha Rao; K. Prathibha Bharathi was the first woman Speaker of the AP Assembly (11th Assembly, 1999-2004).

s:
Consider the following statements about removal motions against Lok Sabha Speakers:
1. G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker to face a removal motion, in 1954.
2. A removal motion against Balram Jakhar was moved in 1966.
3. The 2026 motion against Om Birla was rejected by voice vote.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the 1966 motion was against Hukam Singh; the one against Balram Jakhar was in 1987. All these failed; the motion against Om Birla (signed by 118 Opposition MPs) was rejected by voice vote on 11 Mar 2026.

s:
Match List-I (Power of the Speaker) with List-II (Article):
List-I
a. Decides finally whether a Bill is a Money Bill
b. Endorses his certificate on a Money Bill sent to the Rajya Sabha
c. Exercises a casting vote in a tie
d. Presides over a joint sitting of both Houses
List-II
i. Article 118(4)
ii. Article 100(1)
iii. Article 110(4)
iv. Article 110(3)
x: Money Bill decision – Art. 110(3); certificate – Art. 110(4); casting vote – Art. 100(1); presiding over a joint sitting – Art. 118(4) (the joint sitting itself is summoned under Art. 108).

s:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule are subject to judicial review.
2. The leader of a party having at least one-third of the strength of the House is recognised as Leader of the Opposition.
3. The Speaker decides the admissibility of questions, motions and resolutions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the requirement is one-tenth of the House, not one-third. Anti-defection decisions are subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan, 1992), and admissibility of questions, motions and resolutions is decided by the Speaker under the Rules of Procedure.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Panel of Chairpersons of the Lok Sabha:
1. Its members, up to ten, are nominated by the Speaker.
2. A member of the Panel presides when the office of the Speaker is vacant.
3. If no member of the Panel is present, the House determines who shall preside.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: a Panel member presides only when both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent, not when the Speaker's office is vacant (then the Deputy Speaker performs the duties). If none is present, the House decides (Art. 95(2)).

s:
Consider the following statements about the election of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. Under Article 93, the Lok Sabha chooses the Speaker from among its own members.
2. A person who is not a member may be elected Speaker if he becomes a member within six months.
3. The date of the Speaker's election is fixed by the President.
4. The Speaker takes a separate oath of office as Speaker.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the six-month grace belongs to Ministers (Art. 75(5)); the Speaker must already be a member. Statement 4 is wrong: the Speaker takes only the oath as an MP. The President fixes the date of the Speaker's election (Rule 7).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha addresses his resignation to the Deputy Speaker.
2. A resolution to remove the Speaker must be passed by two-thirds of the members present and voting.
3. At least 14 days' notice is required before such a resolution is moved.
4. The Deputy Speaker too is removed by a resolution of the Lok Sabha under Article 94(c).
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: removal under Art. 94(c) needs a majority of all the then members (effective majority), not two-thirds. The Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker, 14 days' notice is needed, and the same Art. 94(c) applies to the Deputy Speaker.

s:
Assertion (A): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha does not vacate his office when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
Reason (R): On dissolution, the Deputy Speaker also continues in office until the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: the Speaker continues until immediately before the first meeting of the new House (second proviso to Art. 94). R is false: the Deputy Speaker and the members go at once on dissolution.

s:
Consider the following statements about a resolution for the removal of a presiding officer:
1. While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, the Speaker cannot preside even if he is present.
2. During such a resolution the Speaker may vote in the first instance but cannot exercise a casting vote.
3. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, during a resolution for his removal, may vote in the first instance like the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Chairman is not a member of the Rajya Sabha, so he cannot vote at all during his removal resolution (he may only speak). Under Art. 96 the Speaker cannot preside, may speak and vote in the first instance, but has no casting vote.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salaries of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Like the Speaker, a Governor can be removed only after 14 days' notice.
3. In the Warrant of Precedence, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha ranks with the Chief Justice of India, above Cabinet Ministers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: a Governor is removed by the President at will, without notice; 14 days' notice applies to the President, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Deputy Chairman. Art. 97 charges the presiding officers' salaries on the Consolidated Fund; the CJI and Speaker share rank 6, above Cabinet Ministers (rank 7).

s:
Consider the following statements about sessions of Parliament:
1. Six months shall not intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.
2. The Constitution provides for three sessions – Budget, Monsoon and Winter.
3. The Winter session is usually the longest session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the three sessions are a convention; the Constitution fixes no number of sessions. Statement 3 is wrong: the Budget session is the longest and the Winter session the shortest. Art. 85(1) counts six months from the last sitting to the first sitting.

s:
Match List-I (Device) with List-II (Effect):
List-I
a. Adjournment
b. Adjournment sine die
c. Prorogation
d. Dissolution
List-II
i. Ends the life of the House; pending business lapses
ii. Ends the session; pending Bills do not lapse
iii. Terminates a sitting for an indefinite period
iv. Suspends a sitting for hours, days or weeks
x: Adjournment suspends a sitting for a fixed time (session continues); adjournment sine die ends a sitting for an indefinite period; prorogation ends the session but Bills do not lapse; dissolution (LS only) ends the life of the House and pending business lapses (subject to Art. 107).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President prorogues the Houses under Article 85(2)(a) on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
2. On prorogation, pending Bills lapse.
3. After prorogation, only the President can summon the House.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Bills do not lapse on prorogation – only notices lapse (except notices to introduce Bills). Prorogation is by the President under Art. 85(2)(a) on the Council of Ministers' advice, and after it only the President can summon the House.

s:
Consider the following statements about the President's address to Parliament:
1. Under Article 86 the President may send messages to either House about a pending Bill.
2. Under Article 87 the President makes a special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year.
3. The special address is prepared by the President's own Secretariat and does not state the Government's policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the address is prepared by the Union Cabinet and states the Government's policy. Art. 86 – address, require attendance, send messages; Art. 87 – special address after each general election and at the first session of each year.

s:
Assertion (A): Defeat of the Motion of Thanks on the President's address amounts to the defeat of the Government.
Reason (R): The President's address is prepared by the Union Cabinet and states the policy of the Government.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: since the address is the Government's own policy statement, rejecting the Motion of Thanks on it is a defeat of the Government, which must resign.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Chairman votes in the first instance like other members.
3. The Chairman can be removed only by removing him as Vice-President.
4. The Chairman cannot dissolve the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Chairman has only a casting vote in a tie. He is the Vice-President ex officio (Arts. 64, 89(1)), is removed only by removal as VP (Art. 67(b)), and cannot dissolve the RS, which is a permanent House.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. He addresses his resignation to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. He is removed by a resolution under Article 94(c).
3. The Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is nominated by the Deputy Chairman.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Deputy Chairman is removed under Art. 90(c) (Art. 94(c) is for the Speaker/Deputy Speaker). Statement 3 is wrong: the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons is nominated by the Chairman.

s:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Office in the Rajya Sabha):
List-I
a. S. Radhakrishnan
b. Mohammad Hamid Ansari
c. Harivansh
d. P.J. Kurien
List-II
i. Deputy Chairman, 2012-18
ii. First Chairman, 1952-62
iii. Deputy Chairman since August 2018
iv. Chairman, 2007-17
x: S. Radhakrishnan – first Chairman (1952-62); Hamid Ansari – Chairman 2007-17 (two terms); Harivansh – Deputy Chairman since Aug 2018 (re-elected 2020 and Apr 2026); P.J. Kurien – Deputy Chairman 2012-18.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Parliament Secretariat:
1. Article 98 gives each House a separate secretarial staff, though posts common to both Houses may be created.
2. Until Parliament makes a law, the President makes the service rules after consulting the Speaker or the Chairman.
3. The Lok Sabha Secretariat works under the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
4. The Secretary-General of each House is appointed by its presiding officer and holds the rank of Cabinet Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Lok Sabha Secretariat is independent of the executive and works under the direct control of the Speaker. Art. 98(1) and 98(3) are correctly stated, and the Secretary-General is appointed by the presiding officer with the rank of Cabinet Secretary.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The date of the Deputy Speaker's election is fixed by the President.
2. That the Deputy Speaker comes from the Opposition is only a convention.
3. While presiding, the Deputy Speaker has the same powers as the Speaker and no appeal lies to the Speaker against his rulings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Deputy Speaker's election date is fixed by the Speaker (Rule 8) and communicated by the Secretary-General; the President fixes only the Speaker's. The Opposition practice is a convention, and under Art. 95 he is not subordinate to the Speaker.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. He is appointed by the President under Article 95(1).
2. He is elected by the members of the newly elected House.
3. He administers the oath to new members and presides over the election of the Speaker.
4. His tenure ends when the regular Speaker is elected.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Pro-Tem Speaker is not elected; he is appointed and sworn in by the President, usually from the senior-most members. He swears in members, presides over the Speaker's election and goes when the regular Speaker is elected.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. When not in the Chair, he may vote in the first instance like an ordinary member.
2. While a resolution for his own removal is under consideration, he may exercise a casting vote.
3. The last Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha was M. Thambidurai (2014-19).
4. The post has been vacant since June 2014.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: during his own removal resolution he cannot preside and has no casting vote (he may speak and vote in the first instance); the post has been vacant since June 2019, after M. Thambidurai (2014-19).

s:
Consider the following statements about Zero Hour:
1. Zero Hour is provided for in the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha.
2. It is an Indian innovation in use since 1962.
3. Ministers are bound to reply to the matters raised in Zero Hour.
4. In the Lok Sabha it begins immediately after Question Hour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: Zero Hour is informal – neither in the Rules of Procedure nor in the Constitution. Statement 3 is wrong: Ministers are not bound to reply. It is an Indian innovation (since 1962) and starts at 12 Noon, right after Question Hour.

s:
Match List-I (Device and House) with List-II (Timing, since 2014):
List-I
a. Question Hour in the Lok Sabha
b. Zero Hour in the Rajya Sabha
c. Question Hour in the Rajya Sabha
d. Zero Hour in the Lok Sabha
List-II
i. 11 AM – 12 Noon
ii. 12 Noon – 1 PM
iii. 11 AM, opening the day's sitting
iv. From 12 Noon till the regular business is taken up
x: Lok Sabha: Question Hour 11 AM-12 Noon, Zero Hour from 12 Noon until the agenda is taken up. Rajya Sabha (since 2014): the day begins with Zero Hour at 11 AM and Question Hour is 12 Noon-1 PM.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. An ordinary parliamentary question requires 15 clear days' notice.
2. To raise a matter in Zero Hour, a member intimates the Presiding Officer on the same day.
3. Directions given by the Chair in Zero Hour reach the ministry concerned through the Cabinet Secretariat.
4. In the Lok Sabha up to 20 matters a day, in order of the ballot, may be raised in Zero Hour.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: Zero Hour directions reach the ministry through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. 15 clear days' notice applies to an ordinary question, Zero Hour needs only same-day intimation, and 20 balloted matters a day may be raised in the Lok Sabha.

s:
Consider the following statements about the no-confidence motion:
1. It is expressly provided for in Article 75(3) of the Constitution.
2. It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
3. It is directed against the entire Council of Ministers.
4. Leave to move it needs the support of at least 100 members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Constitution mentions neither a confidence nor a no-confidence motion – it only flows from Art. 75(3) (collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha). Statement 4 is wrong: 50 members are needed. It is moved only in the Lok Sabha against the whole Council of Ministers.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In November 1954 Gouthu Latchanna's no-confidence motion against the Prakasam ministry of Andhra State was carried 69–68.
2. President's Rule was imposed in Andhra State from November 1954.
3. The first no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha was moved by J.B. Kripalani against Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963.
4. Notice of a no-confidence motion is given in writing to the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 4 is wrong: written notice of a no-confidence motion goes to the Secretary-General (the Speaker then decides admissibility). The Prakasam ministry fell by one vote (69–68) in Nov 1954 and President's Rule followed; Kripalani moved the first motion against Nehru in 1963.

s:
Match List-I (Motion) with List-II (Feature):
List-I
a. No-confidence motion
b. Censure motion
c. Confidence motion
d. Privilege motion
List-II
i. Reasons must be stated; ministers are not bound to resign
ii. No reasons needed; if passed, the Council of Ministers must resign
iii. Referred to the Committee of Privileges
iv. Moved by the Government to prove its majority
x: No-confidence: no reasons, against the whole CoM, which must resign if it passes. Censure: reasons must be stated and it is only disapproval. Confidence: moved by the Government in the Lok Sabha; if defeated the Government falls. Privilege motion: referred to the Committee of Privileges.

s:
Assertion (A): A Prime Minister who is a member of the Rajya Sabha cannot vote in the Lok Sabha even on a no-confidence motion against his own government.
Reason (R): The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the PM cannot vote because he is not a member of the Lok Sabha; collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha (Art. 75(3)) is why the motion is moved there, not why he cannot vote.

s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary control over the executive:
1. Question Hour, supplementary questions and adjournment motions together form the 'accountability triangle'.
2. A walkout is one of the instruments of parliamentary control.
3. Question Hour is considered the most effective method of keeping day-to-day vigil on the executive.
4. Dissolution of the House is a tool of parliamentary control.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: a walkout is a protest, not an instrument, and dissolution is an executive power. The four instruments are deliberation, approval or refusal of laws, financial control and the no-confidence motion; Question Hour is the most effective day-to-day vigil.

s:
Consider the following statements about the adjournment motion:
1. It can be moved in either House of Parliament.
2. It needs the support of 50 members for admission.
3. The debate on it lasts not less than two hours and thirty minutes.
4. More than one adjournment motion may be taken up at a sitting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the adjournment motion is a Lok Sabha device (the Rajya Sabha cannot use it). Statement 4 is wrong: not more than one such motion at a sitting. It needs the Presiding Officer's consent and 50 members, and the debate lasts at least 2 h 30 min.

s:
Assertion (A): A calling attention motion carries no element of censure of the Government.
Reason (R): A calling attention motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: it only seeks an authoritative statement from a Minister and does not disrupt business. R is false: a calling attention motion can be moved in either House; it is the adjournment motion that is confined to the Lok Sabha.

s:
Consider the following statements about the calling attention device:
1. It was introduced in 1954.
2. A member may give not more than one calling attention notice for a sitting.
3. Calling attention notices restricted the scope of the adjournment motion.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: a member may give not more than two notices for a sitting (notices in writing by 10 AM). The device dates from 1954 and it narrowed the use of the adjournment motion.

s:
Match List-I (Closure) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I
a. Simple closure
b. Closure by compartments
c. Kangaroo closure
d. Guillotine
List-II
i. All remaining clauses or demands are put to vote when the allotted time is over
ii. Only important clauses are debated; intervening clauses are taken as passed
iii. Clauses are grouped into parts and debated and voted part by part
iv. The matter is declared sufficiently discussed and put to vote
x: Simple closure – 'sufficiently discussed, be now put to vote'; compartments – part by part; kangaroo – only important clauses, the rest taken as passed; guillotine – remaining clauses/demands put to vote, discussed or not, when the time ends.

s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary questions:
1. A starred question is marked with an asterisk and is answered orally.
2. Supplementary questions are allowed on unstarred questions.
3. A short notice question may be asked with less than 10 days' notice on a matter of urgent public importance.
4. At most 20 starred questions are listed a day for oral answer.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: an unstarred question gets a written answer and no supplementaries; supplementaries are allowed on starred and short notice questions. The other three are as in the notes.

s:
Match List-I (Type of question) with List-II (Colour of paper):
List-I
a. Starred question
b. Unstarred question
c. Short notice question
d. Question to a private member
List-II
i. Yellow
ii. Light pink
iii. White
iv. Green
x: Starred – green; unstarred – white; short notice – light pink; question to a private member – yellow (not blue).

s:
Match List-I (Rule of the Lok Sabha) with List-II (Device):
List-I
a. Rule 184
b. Rule 193
c. Rule 377
d. Rule 198
List-II
i. No-confidence motion
ii. Special mention
iii. Short-duration discussion without voting
iv. Discussion with a formal motion and voting
x: Rule 184 – discussion with a formal motion and voting; Rule 193 – short-duration discussion, no motion or vote; Rule 377 – special mention; Rule 198 – no-confidence motion.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A short-duration discussion under Rule 193 lasts at most two hours.
2. A matter under Rule 377 is raised after written notice to the Secretary-General and with the Speaker's consent.
3. Special Mentions in the Rajya Sabha are made under Rules 180A–E.
4. A privilege motion is raised under Rule 222 in the Rajya Sabha and Rule 187 in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
x: Statement 4 reverses the Houses: a privilege motion is under Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha. Rule 193 discussions last a maximum of 2 hours; Rule 377 needs written notice and the Speaker's consent; RS Special Mentions are under Rules 180A–E.

s:
Consider the following statements about a privilege motion:
1. It is moved when a Minister withholds facts of a case or gives distorted facts.
2. It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
3. It is referred to the Committee of Privileges.
4. If adopted, it forces the Government to resign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: a privilege motion can be moved in either House. Statement 4 is wrong: it aims to censure the minister and does not force the Government to resign. It is a breach-of-privilege device referred to the Committee of Privileges.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Whip:
1. The office of Whip rests on parliamentary conventions, not on the Constitution or the Rules.
2. The 1998 Act on Leaders and Chief Whips put the office of Whip into the Rules of Procedure.
3. The Government Chief Whip in the Lok Sabha is the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs.
4. A two-line whip directs members to vote strictly as the party directs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the 1998 Act only gives facilities. Statement 4 is wrong: a two-line whip is a direction to attend; the three-line whip directs members to vote strictly as the party directs (one-line is informative).

s:
Consider the following statements about resolutions in Parliament:
1. A resolution is always a substantive motion.
2. The mover can withdraw it only by leave of the House.
3. A resolution on the same subject is barred for six months.
4. Private members' resolutions are taken up on alternate Fridays in the afternoon sitting.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: the same subject is barred for one year, not six months. The rest are as in the notes.
